nodes.summary: `g₁ ≤cx g₂` if `∫ φ dg₁ ≤ ∫ φ dg₂` for every convex `φ : ℝ → ℝ` that is integrable under both laws (Shaked–Shanthikumar 2007, §3.A).
nodes.title: Convex order

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `renewal_exp_iff`, exponential growth at rate `r` solves the renewal equation iff `R = 1 / M_g(-r)`.
nodes.title: Euler–Lotka

nodes.summary: For `c ≠ 0`, the exponential `b(t) = c e^{r t}` solves `b(t) = R ∫ b(t - a) g(da)` for every `t` iff `R M_g(-r) = 1`. This is meaningful when `a ↦ e^{-r a}` is `g`-integrable; otherwise Lean's integral and `M_g(-r)` are both `0` and both sides of the equivalence are false.
nodes.title: Renewal equation for exponential growth

nodes.summary: Fixed generation interval `T`: `R = e^{r T}` (for all real `r`, `T`).
nodes.title: Fixed generation interval

nodes.summary: Exponential generation interval with mean `T > 0` (rate `1 / T`): for `r T > -1`, `R = 1 + r T` (Wallinga–Lipsitch 2007, eq. 3.1).
nodes.title: Exponential generation interval

nodes.summary: Gamma generation interval with shape `α > 0` and rate `β > 0`: for `r > -β`, `R = (1 + r / β)^α`.
nodes.title: Gamma generation interval

nodes.summary: If the generation interval has finite mean `T̄ = ∫ a g(da)` and finite `M_g(-r)`, then `R ≤ e^{r T̄}` (any real `r`); Wallinga and Lipsitch (2007, §3) note that the fixed interval gives this upper bound.
nodes.title: Jensen bound

nodes.summary: If `g₁ ≤cx g₂` and both have finite `M(-r)`, then `R(g₂) ≤ R(g₁)` at growth rate `r` (any real `r`). In particular, among generation intervals with a given mean, the fixed interval maximizes `R`.
nodes.title: More spread lowers `R`

nodes.summary: The reproductive number is positive when `M_g(-r)` is finite.
nodes.title: Positivity of the reproductive number

nodes.summary: The reproductive number implied by growth rate `r` and generation-interval law `g`: `R = 1 / M_g(-r)` (Wallinga–Lipsitch 2007, eq. 2.9).
nodes.title: Reproductive number from growth rate and generation interval

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
